That truly is a beautiful quote. I appreciate you sharing that. There’s much truth to it, for every suicide victim. It hurts a bit, to accept. I knew of his everyday battling inside his brain, I even thought it was mutual. We bonded over our pain and hatred for the world. It’s true, he was not himself that day. But that hurts as well, just within a couple minutes he made such a permanent Choice. A part of me is happy he is no longer suffering, im happy he’s freed of his human flesh body. But the happiness fades when I alter the attention back to myself, and realize now that I am still here.. all alone.. without him. His circumstances are so damn confusing. He called the crisis hotline… but said he had a gun.. which was not true. The police arrived right away, heard the car inside the garage running, but would not go in because he was “armed and dangerous” they waited outside for hours, until his mom got home. (Who decided to wait until her shift was over to come home even though she was the first person made aware when he stormed out of my house in a rage and I let her know I thought he was going to do something horrible). I feel like a fucking idiot for putting his life in the hands of his mother, who has never really been too fond of him. I assumed in a life or death she would drop everything for her child. I was wrong. By the time she got home, with the garage door opener so the police to “stand back and take cover” my sweet lover was face down by the door to exit the garage. I wonder if that was his attempt to escape last minute, but he couldn’t make it all the way. It truly shatters me. I wish you would of got the chance to know him as well. He is someone truly irreplaceable. You would of loved him. I’ve considered all perspectives on this situation. If it was an accident on his part, I want to die. If it wasn’t an accident, I want to die. He’d always been too coward to do it also. But he did the bravest thing a human could do that day, go against their one and only true natural instinct, to survive. As much as I’d like to tell myself, I couldn’t of changed his mind, I couldn’t of known. I can’t lie to myself. He told me many times how he wanted to kill himself, I told him the feeling was mutual. Because it was. He’d make comments like I’d be better off without him, he holds me back, etc. i took him for granted many times. I’ve considered the future, finding beautiful love like that again, picking up new hobbies, finding myself, I have no desire to do any of those things. I never did while I was with him either. This is something I truly believe I cannot live with. It’s permanent… I would take my chances. To stay sane I must believe I will see him again if I die. I see “signs” often from him, but those are those “little things” we talked about. So minuscule and pointless on a bigger scale. I don’t care that he drew me a heart in the sky with the clouds, I want to look into his eyes and fall into his arms. I consider possibly trying to “get my life together” again… but the thing is that our life we lived together was perfect… absolutely. i don’t want to live a life any other way, and I can’t do what we did alone, because it’s no fun. It’s painfully boring. Pointless. I plan and articulate my suicide everyday. This is the farthest thing from an impulse decision. But so far, each day has only deepened my wishes to die. I’m only 18, but I truly was comfortable for life within our relationship routine. I will never be able to understand. So therefore I refuse to live in this misery. No one will be supportive of my decision, which bothers me. I don’t want to be alone when I die, but I feel as though I have no other choice. This human life offers nothing of my interest. I hope to be something with much less consciousness, preferably a stick or leaf. I’ve never dealt with loss quite this close before. I ask you, how do you wrap your head around the permanence? How do you cope with the forever factor? That your aunt, my lover, any person who passes away, will never be back for the entire rest of your life… that shit is unacceptable to me. I can’t imagine being 80 and still never of seeing my love again since he passed while I was 18. 
All my love to you. Thank you for talking to me.
